findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how Cloud convergence is guaranteed for the ~0.35% of bodies that are NOT round-trip-idempotent under Jira ADF re-canonicalization (the compare at outbound_field_diff.py:292 decodes only the remote, so a recanon miss re-emits every pass, not once) — e.g. decode BOTH the fitted-local and the remote through the codec on compare so a benign recanon is absorbed, or add a bounded/sha-gated re-emit guard — and cover it in test_recanonicalization_converges.
evidence: Plan: 'terminates iff the codec is idempotent under the compare — guaranteed by the codec law ... plus the empirically-proven round-trip idempotence (marklas 99.65%)'

Plan: 'a benign Jira re-canonicalization is absorbed by the decode-on-compare, then converges on the next pass' — but the compare decodes only the REMOTE (fitted local is compared to it), and 0.35% of ADF bodies are not recanon-invariant under adf_to_markdown

Code: outbound_field_diff.py:287-292 deliberately compares against the RAW remote (decoded once); outbound_fields.py:555-561 documents the same raw-remote compare — neither re-normalizes the remote to absorb an idempotence miss
findings.finding: The Cloud once-only-re-emit convergence claim is unsound for the residual non-round-trip-idempotent fraction of bodies the plan itself cites (marklas 99.65% ⇒ ~0.35% non-idempotent). For those bodies, after the push the refetched ADF is Jira's re-canonicalized form, and the raw-decoded remote compared at outbound_field_diff.py:292 never equals the fitted local — so the description re-emits on EVERY pass, not 'exactly once', producing the churn loop the story is meant to prevent. (DC converges unconditionally because decode_inbound is identity and both sides derive from the same markdown via the same renderer; the gap is Cloud-specific.)
findings.location: Prior art §'Once-only re-emit convergence already exists'; Approach step 1; AC 'test_recanonicalization_converges'
scenarios: A Markdown body whose ADF is re-canonicalized by Jira such that adf_to_markdown of the stored form differs from normalize_outbound(local) — re-emits a description update on every reconcile pass indefinitely
findings.suggested_fix: For the description compare after the Cloud cutover, normalize BOTH operands through decode_inbound(to_wire(·)) (or compare on the decoded-markdown projection of the remote rather than the raw remote) so a Jira re-canonicalization that survives one decode is absorbed and the field converges within one re-emit even when strict round-trip idempotence does not hold; state the termination argument in terms of the decoded-compare fixpoint, not raw round-trip idempotence.
